summary: Frontend-only end-to-end test of the Members Management (Team) iteration. All Supabase-driven flows work correctly. Verified against live preview URL with two fresh Supabase accounts (OWNER=hqowner1788824025@gmail.com, OPERATOR=hqoperator1788824025@gmail.com, Test1234!). PASSED: (1) OWNER signup runs migration (38 records / 12 tables) then lands on Home. (2) More tab shows Team card with both open-team-btn and invite-team-btn (owner-only). Account card role chip = OWNER. (3) /team header shows 'Owner Farm Test' + '1 member · 0 pending invites'. invite-card testID visible. Owner appears in Active Members with OWNER badge. (4) Sending invite (role=operator) shows success notice, count flips to '1 member · 1 pending invite', pending row with Resend + Revoke buttons for the invited email is listed. (5) OPERATOR signs up with the exact invited email + a business name that is intentionally ignored: NO migration screen, lands straight on Home. Machinery tab shows OWNER's fleet: Case 340 (5210h, Overdue), Big Rig (2380h, Due Soon), Hardi Commander (1980h, Good) - proving accept_pending_invitations RPC ran during bootstrap and the operator joined the OWNER's business rather than creating a new one. Home shows OWNER's Service Reminders (Case 340 Overdue, Big Rig Due Soon). (6) OPERATOR More tab: role chip = OPERATOR, invite-team-btn is ABSENT. /team screen: invite-card is ABSENT, both members listed (owner shown as OWNER, operator shown as OPERATOR '(you)'), no promote/demote/remove buttons on the owner row, footer 'Only the owner can invite or remove team members and change roles.' visible. (7) OWNER signs back in: pending invitation row is gone (correctly consumed), both members are under Active Members. Owner sees Promote-to-Manager + Remove buttons on the operator row and NONE on their own (isMe) row. NOT VERIFIABLE via web preview (see critical issue): the destructive confirmation Alert.alert (Remove member, Revoke invitation, Sign out) is a no-op in react-native-web 0.21.2, so we could not exercise the terminal 'Remove operator', 'Revoke invite', or in-app 'Sign out' paths through the UI. Immediate-access-loss step (operator's machinery becomes empty after removal) therefore could not be end-to-end verified on web, but Supabase RLS is standard so this is expected to work on native builds where Alert.alert renders a real dialog.

ui_bugs.issue: react-native-web@0.21.2 ships Alert.alert as a no-op (see /app/frontend/node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js). This means the destructive confirm dialogs for Remove member (team.tsx:63), Revoke invitation (team.tsx:78), Delete Machine (machinery/[id].tsx:96), Delete Schedule (machinery/[id].tsx:286) and Sign out (more.tsx:32) do nothing on the web preview - the destructive callback never fires. On native (iOS/Android via Expo Go or dev builds) this works correctly. If the web preview is treated as a shipping surface, replace Alert.alert with a cross-platform confirm (custom Modal on web, Alert.alert on native, or expo-router's platform-specific split).

action_items: Wrap Alert.alert destructive confirms in a platform-aware helper. On web use a Modal (or window.confirm as a minimal shim) so Remove member, Revoke invite and Sign out actually execute. Without this, users on the deployed web preview can never sign out, remove a member, or revoke an invite via the UI.
Consider persisting the migration-complete marker in Supabase (e.g. business_members.migrated_at) so it survives web browser context switches - noted in iter_10 too. Not a blocker for this iteration.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/team.tsx and /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/more.tsx both rely on Alert.alert with buttons - that API is a no-op in react-native-web@0.21.2 (dist/exports/Alert/index.js contains static alert() {}). This silently breaks destructive flows on web.

members.ts:47 (updateRole) and members.ts:56 (remove) rely entirely on RLS to gate mutations. This is fine, but the client also does not check role in changeRole/confirmRemove before firing the request - a hostile client would just receive a 4xx from PostgREST. UI already hides the buttons for non-owners so it's belt-and-braces only.
auth-context.tsx:90 correctly gates migration to (isFreshBusiness && acceptedInvites === 0 && !already). This is what makes the two-account flow work end-to-end. Verified live.

invite email dedupe: team.tsx:43 lowercases and compares against members list but not against pending invites - inviting an already-pending email again would call the upsert path which is fine, but a friendlier UX would tell the owner 'already invited'.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (all read + create paths pass; destructive Alert paths not testable on web due to rn-web Alert no-op)

seed_data_creation: Created 2 live Supabase accounts for this run: hqowner1788824025@gmail.com (business_id owned = Owner Farm Test, role=owner) and hqoperator1788824025@gmail.com (joined via invitation, role=operator). Password 'Test1234!'. One pending invite was created and auto-consumed on operator signup. No deletions were possible because the Remove confirmation dialog is a no-op on web.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Team feature works end-to-end on web preview EXCEPT the destructive Alert.alert flows (Remove/Revoke/Sign-out) - react-native-web 0.21.2 has Alert.alert stubbed to a no-op. To sign a user out during a test just clear supabase localStorage keys and reload: `Object.keys(localStorage).forEach(k=>{if(k.includes('supabase')||k.includes('sb-'))localStorage.removeItem(k)}); location.reload();`. For future runs use unique @gmail.com addresses per test (Supabase rejects non-real TLDs). testIDs on /team: invite-card, invite-email, role-operator, role-manager, send-invite-btn, team-notice, team-error, invite-row-<id>, resend-<id>, revoke-<id>, member-row-<uid>, member-role-<uid>, promote-<uid>, demote-<uid>, remove-<uid>. testIDs on /more: account-card, sign-out-btn, open-team-btn, invite-team-btn. IMPORTANT ORDER: OWNER must send the invite BEFORE the OPERATOR account signs up, otherwise the accept_pending_invitations RPC returns 0 and the operator creates their own business.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of destructive-action inability on web: react-native-web@0.21.2 (installed in /app/frontend/node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Alert/index.js) implements Alert as `class Alert { static alert() {} }` - a completely empty stub. Any Alert.alert(title, msg, buttons) call therefore never invokes the confirm-button onPress handler on the web preview. Impact: Remove member, Revoke invite, Sign out, Delete machine and Delete schedule are silently dead on web. Fix: introduce a lightweight platform-conditional helper e.g. `export const confirmDestructive = (title, msg, onOk) => Platform.OS === 'web' ? (window.confirm(`${title}\n\n${msg}`) && onOk()) : Alert.alert(title, msg, [{text:'Cancel',style:'cancel'},{text:'OK',style:'destructive',onPress:onOk}])` and swap the four call sites.
